test: For each order/remake job, find the latest drawing revision for its part with received_on <= job release day and the latest with released_on <= release day. Classify jobs: (a) current (revision_issued = latest received), (b) in release-lag window (issued = latest released but a newer revision was received and not yet released), (c) other mismatch (issued older than latest released). Compare per-job rates of 'wrong revision' scrap reports/pieces and fit/dimension/nonconforming returns across classes, with denominators, by year and customer; check the share of all wrong-revision scrap and returns sitting on classes (b)+(c). Also check ECO-linked jobs.
support: Jobs in class (b) or (c) carry a majority of wrong-revision scrap reports and fit/dimension returns, with per-job rates several times class (a), holding across years.
weaken: Most wrong-revision scrap and fit/dimension returns sit on class (a) jobs (revision_issued was current), or rates are similar across classes.
expect: Moderate confidence that it supports: the data looks generated with a revision-lag mechanism (158 mismatches vs 32,372, uniform turnaround), so I expect wrong-revision scrap concentrated on lag/mismatch jobs, but returns for fit/dimension probably mostly on current-revision jobs (other causes). Since wrong-revision scrap is only 137 reports, sample sizes will be small; I expect a strong ratio but limited dollar size (~$0.05M/yr).
